hints: Notice both pH values are well above 7, so think about which type of compound could release hydroxide ions into water.
Sulfates of Group 2 metals give roughly neutral solutions, while hydroxides give strongly alkaline solutions, so V and W must be hydroxides.
Remember solubility of Group 2 hydroxides increases down the group, so link higher solubility to more hydroxide ions and the higher pH of 13.6.
walkthrough:
**Decide the type of compound from pH**

Both solutions are alkaline. V has pH 13.6 and W has pH 9.4.

That tells us lots of $\text{OH}^-$ ions must be present:
$$\text{X(OH)}_2(\text{s}) \rightleftharpoons \text{X}^{2+}(\text{aq}) + 2\text{OH}^-(\text{aq})$$

**Rule out the sulfates**

Group 2 sulfates like $\text{BaSO}_4$ and $\text{MgSO}_4$ do not produce $\text{OH}^-$ ions when they dissolve.

They give neutral or only slightly acidic solutions, around pH 6 to 7, never pH 9 to 14.

**Use the solubility trend for hydroxides**

Solubility of Group 2 hydroxides increases down the group. So $\text{Ba(OH)}_2$ is much more soluble than $\text{Mg(OH)}_2$.

More dissolved solid means higher $[\text{OH}^-]$ and higher pH:
$$\text{more soluble} \rightarrow \text{more } \text{OH}^- \rightarrow \text{higher pH}$$

**Match V and W**

V has the very high pH of 13.6, so it must be the more soluble hydroxide containing barium.

W has the lower pH of 9.4, so it must be the sparingly soluble hydroxide containing magnesium.

options.A: Incorrect. Both $\text{BaSO}_4$ and $\text{MgSO}_4$ are sulfates and do not release $\text{OH}^-$ ions. They cannot give pH 13.6 and 9.4.
options.B: Incorrect. This is the same sulfate trap in reverse. $\text{MgSO}_4$ solution is slightly acidic and $\text{BaSO}_4$ is essentially insoluble and neutral, so neither matches the strongly alkaline pH values.
options.C: Correct. Both are hydroxides, which explains the alkaline pH values. $\text{Ba(OH)}_2$ is soluble and gives the very alkaline pH 13.6 for V, while $\text{Mg(OH)}_2$ is sparingly soluble and gives the weakly alkaline pH 9.4 for W.
options.D: Incorrect. The compounds are the right type but the wrong way round. $\text{Mg(OH)}_2$ is far less soluble than $\text{Ba(OH)}_2$, so it cannot give the higher pH of 13.6.
